After another quick postseason exit, Philadelphia Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski acknowledged that the club needs to improve its offensive production at several positions, while also addressing some of the depth concerns that emerged during the past campaign.
 One particularly interesting situation involves the catching position. Although the Phillies re-signed veteran backstop J.T. Realmuto and continued to rely on him for a leading workload, Dombrowski has noted that the team has decided to reduce the number of games he catches going forward. That has made finding another dependable option behind the plate an clear offseason priority.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement And now, the Phillies have now reportedly taken a step toward addressing that situation by acquiring a recent San Diego Padres castoff.
 "The Phillies are reportedly signing C Blake Hunt to a minor league contract with an invite to Spring Training," Phillies Report noted last week , citing Paragon Sports International agent Garrett Parcell, among the other outlets confirming the news.
 Cubs' Massive 4-Year Southpaw Castoff Joins AL West After Latest Cut 
 Philadelphia Phillies Add Former San Diego Padres Catcher With JT Realmuto's Role Changing
 The reported addition came shortly after Dombrowski publicly discussed his decision to reduce Realmuto's workload after several years as one of baseball's most utilized catchers.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "At the Phillies' year-end press conference … president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski discussed a recent conversation he had with Realmuto, whom the organization re-signed to a three-year, $45 million contract last winter," Cole Weintraub recalled for NBC Sports Philadelphia . "Dombrowski called Realmuto before the press conference because he did not want him to learn publicly that the Phillies intend to reduce his workload next season."
 Realmuto remains an important part of Philadelphia's plans, but the organization needs to find someone capable of handling more responsibility behind the plate.
 The team has previously relied on the combination of Rafael Marchan and Garrett Stubbs as backup options, but it cut ties with Stubbs shortly after the season ended and Marchan has struggled to stay healthy. However, finding additional competition could give manager Don Mattingly more flexibility while keeping Realmuto fresher throughout the season.
 Cardinals Castoff Zach Plesac Attempts Surprise Two-Way Return After Cut 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Philadelphia Phillies' New Catcher Blake Hunt Could Bring Key Depth After San Diego Padres Cut
 Hunt, 27, arrives with considerable professional experience despite having a relatively limited major-league resume.
 Originally selected by the San Diego Padres in the second round of the 2017 MLB Draft, Hunt spent time in the Tampa Bay Rays, Seattle Mariners and Baltimore Orioles organizations before returning to the Padres.
 "He has a solid defensive reputation from his time in the minors but his big league track record consists of just three plate appearances and he struck out in all three of those," Darragh McDonald wrote for MLB Trade Rumors . "He has been a decent bat in the minors, with a combined .259/.339/.467 line dating back to the start of 2023, which includes a .301/.381/.617 line this year."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Hunt made his major-league debut with San Diego in June 2026 after spending years working his way through the minor leagues. However, his opportunity was brief, and the Padres released him in September.
 The reported minor-league agreement gives Hunt an opportunity to compete for a place in Philadelphia's catching picture during Spring Training. It does not guarantee him a spot on the major-league roster, but it gives the Phillies another option as they attempt to reduce Realmuto's responsibilities.
 This article was originally published on Forbes.com
